memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "At midday you will grope about like a blind person in the dark. You will be unsuccessful in everything you do... You will be pledged to be married to a woman, but another will take her and rape her. You will build a house, but you will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will not even begin to enjoy its fruit... Your sons and daughters will be given to another nation, and you will wear out your eyes watching for them day after day, powerless to lift a hand." — Deut 28:29-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This section describes a particular kind of anguish — labouring hard and never enjoying the fruit. You build a house but never live in it; plant a vineyard but never taste its wine; even your own children taken from you as you watch helplessly. It is the misery of effort without reward, of life's deepest hopes snatched away. This was among the covenant consequences God warned would come with persistent rebellion.

There is a haunting truth beneath these images: sin ultimately robs. It promises satisfaction and delivers emptiness. The path away from God may look appealing at first, but it cannot finally deliver joy. It leaves a person groping "at midday" — lost even when the light should be clearest.

We do not read this as our covenant curse, but the underlying reality remains sobering. A life lived apart from God, however busy and productive, cannot secure lasting joy. As Jesus asked, what does it profit someone to gain the whole world yet lose their soul? (Mark 8:36)

The gospel offers the opposite of this curse. In Christ, our labour is never finally in vain (1 Cor 15:58). Even now, He gives meaning to our work, and He promises a future where every tear is wiped away and no joy is ever snatched from us again. What sin steals, Christ restores. Build your life on Him, and your deepest hopes are secure.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I chasing satisfaction anywhere that cannot finally deliver it?
2. How does Christ give lasting meaning to my everyday work?
3. What hope does the promise of restored joy give me today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, guard me from chasing empty things that cannot satisfy. Thank You that in Christ my labour is not in vain and my deepest hopes are secure in You. Restore my joy. Amen.
